questions.question:
Fill in the blank :

The autumn _______ of parliament will begin on Monday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"session". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"session" **refers to a period devoted to a particular activity or a meeting or series of meetings of a legislative or judicial body for the purpose of executing its duties.
 
• In the context of parliament, **"session" **is the most appropriate choice as it signifies the scheduled period during which the parliament meets to conduct its business.
 
• **"Session" **is spelled correctly as per the given options and is the term widely used in governmental and legislative contexts.
 
• The context of the sentence indicates a time-bound event related to a governing body, which aligns perfectly with the meaning of **"session."**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cession (Option 2) **refers to the formal giving up of rights, property, or territory, usually by a state.

 
 
• It is not suitable for the given blank because it does not relate to a period of meeting or activity.
 
 
 
• **Sesion (Option 3)** is not a correct spelling in English for any word that fits the context of the given sentence.
 
• **Cesión (Option 4)** is also not a correct choice; including that it resembles a misspelling or a word from another language that doesn’t fit the context of a parliamentary meeting period.

questions.question:
**__Direction__: Choose the option that is in the direct form of the sentence.**

She asked him if he would join her on her trip to Manali.

options.text: ​She asked him, "Will I be joining you on my trip to Manali?"
​She asked him, "Will you join to him on his trip to Manali?"
​She asked him, "Will you be joining her on his trip to Manali?"
She asked him, "Will you join me on my trip to Manali?"

questions.solution:
The direct form of the given sentence is** 'She asked him, "Will you join me on my trip to Manali?"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• While changing an **interrogative sentence** from indirect speech to direct speech, we need to follow these steps-

 
 
• The conjunction 'if' is replaced with a comma (,) and inverted commas (" ").
 
• 'Asked' remains either unchanged or changed into 'said to'.
 
• The full stop (.) is changed into the question mark (?).
 
• '**Would**' is changed into '**will**'.
 
• The third-person (he) is changed into (you) i.e. according to the object of the reporting verb (him).
 
• The **possessive adjective (her)** is changed into** 'my' ** and the **third-person (her)** is changed into **(me)** i.e. according to the **subject** of the **reporting verb** (She).

 
 
 

**The final sentence-** *She asked him, "Will you join me on my trip to Manali?"*

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Loss of habitat drives most extinctions because when farms or roads carve forests or fields into fragments, the isolated survivors are more likely to be wiped out.

B. Now, a new study suggests connecting these patches with corridors of suitable habitat can help save populations and species—far more than scientists ever thought.

C. But just 3% of the original ecosystem is left, and what remains exists only as small fragments. 

D. The scientists have concentrated on the grassland habitat for the study, which hosts many unique plants, such as blazing stars, and also the more common butterfly milkweed (above), as well as the endangered red-cockaded woodpecker.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ABDC'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual__ connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 

__
 
• Sentence A is the independent sentence and introduces the topic under discussion – ‘extinction due to habitat loss’ and the why and how behind its cause. 
 
• So, sentence A is the first sentence after rearrangement. 
 
• Sentence B points out a ‘new study’ related to the same topic. So, the second sentence is B to maintain continuity. Hence, B follows A.__
 
• Sentence D points out the study area for the scientists in the new study. So, sentence D should come in the third position.
 
• Sentence C is the concluding statement of the passage as it points out the dangerous situation in which the grassland exists. 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is option 1 i.e. ABDC.

So, the correct paragraph is : ***(A) Loss of habitat drives most extinctions because when farms or roads carve forests or fields into fragments, the isolated survivors are more likely to be wiped out. (B) Now, a new study suggests connecting these patches with corridors of suitable habitat can help save populations and species—far more than scientists ever thought. ​(D) The scientists have concentrated on the grassland habitat for the study, which hosts many unique plants, such as blazing stars, and also the more common butterfly milkweed (above), as well as the endangered red-cockaded woodpecker. (C) But just 3% of the original ecosystem is left, and what remains exists only as small fragments. ***

 ​

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order forming a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. I had reached the most exciting part of my Agatha Christie novel.

B. He was presently gruelling the Duchess seated in the arm chair.

C. Hercule Poirot had managed to get together all his suspects in one room and in his great style was cornering them into confession.

D. She had become extremely nervous and was on the verge of a breakdown.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**ACBD**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
 
• Sentence A will be the first sentence because it contains the main idea of the para jumble. It tells us about an exciting part of 'Agatha Christie novel'.
 
• Sentence C will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence and further tells us the story of the novel and Hercule Poirot.
 
• Sentence B will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence.
 
• Lastly, Sentence D will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• A: I had reached the most exciting part of my Agatha Christie novel.
 
• C: Hercule Poirot had managed to get together all his suspects in one room and in his great style was cornering them into confession.
 
• B: He was presently gruelling the Duchess seated in the arm chair.
 
• D: She had become extremely nervous and was on the verge of a breakdown.

 
 
 
 
 

Correct Sequence:__* I had reached the most exciting part of my Agatha Christie novel. Hercule Poirot had managed to get together all his suspects in one room and in his great style was cornering them into confession. He was presently gruelling the Duchess seated in the arm chair. She had become extremely nervous and was on the verge of a breakdown.*

questions.question: Please keep to the left. (Change into passive voice).

options.text: You are requested to keep it to the left.
Let us keeping to the left.
You should all have kept to the left.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**You are requested to keep it to the left**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The '**voice**'** **of a verb tells us **whether the subject of the sentence performs or receives the action**.
 
• The given sentence is an **imperative **one and is in the **active voice**.
 
• An imperative sentence can be made passive in two ways: one by starting with '*let*,' other by starting with '*you are ordered/requested*.'**
 It usually depends on the tone of the sentence and the focus of the emphasis.
 
 
• For example, *Help me*. (A) ⇒ *Let me be helped*. or *You are requested to help me*. (P)
 
 
 
• The given sentence is a simple instruction that can be interpreted as a request (use of 'Please' hints at it). It means remain on the left-most side (of something, especially a road or path)**.
 
• The best passive form of the given sentence is: ***You are requested to keep it to the left***.

*Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1**.*
